clue.text: Intercept a graduate on island (South American)

parts.note: a BSc is a Bachelor of Science, a graduate's degree
SA is the abbreviation for South America or South American

explanation.surface: A traveller with a degree is waylaid on some South American island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intercept' looks like a verb, but it is the noun from coordinate geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: In coordinate geometry the horizontal coordinate of a point, where a line meets the x-axis, is named by this mathematical term.

clue.text: Period when policemen rioted, head of Met having been dismissed

indicators.note: letters that have rioted are thrown into disorder, signalling a rearrangement
being dismissed means a letter is sent away and removed from the word before it
the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An era when officers ran amok after the Metropolitan Police chief was sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: Take M (head of Met) out of POLICEMEN to leave POLICEEN, then 'rioted' rearranges it. The Met is London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: A geological epoch, the last of the Tertiary, is a period of time in the earth's history.

clue.text: Lack of worldly wisdom ruled out in financiers

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other here

parts.note: the City is London's financial district, standing for its financiers

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Naivety is said to be banned among bankers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruled out' reads as excluded, but 'out' is an anagram signal; the City of London is the UK's finance district, standing for its financiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gullibility, a readiness to believe anything, shows a want of worldly experience.

clue.text: Being in charge, I dropped actor Tom like a stone

indicators.note: dropped means the letter is let fall out of the word

parts.note: Tom Conti is a Scottish stage and film actor
a rolling stone, from the proverb that gathers no moss

explanation.surface: A director boasts of firing a famous actor without ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' removes I from CONTI to give CONT; 'like a stone' leads to ROLLING via the proverb, not to sinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercising control or command over something is the state of being in charge.

clue.text: Leave script in Birkenhead Library

indicators.note: in tells the solver the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a manuscript in a public library on Merseyside.
explanation.walkthrough: Birkenhead is a town on Merseyside across the river from Liverpool; the answer runs across 'BirkenheAD LIBrary'.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise is to depart from a prepared text, speaking without notes.

clue.text: King Arthur? My foot!

definitions.meaning: the Arthur of Camelot is a figure of myth and old story, perhaps never real
read cryptically, a foot is the end of a leg

explanation.walkthrough: 'My foot!' sounds like an exclamation of disbelief, apt for a mythical king, but it splits into the bottom end of a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional story of a heroic figure, perhaps unhistorical, is a myth or tale of this kind.

clue.text: Retreat from tree before collision

indicators.note: before places the tree ahead of the collision in the answer

parts.note: the ash is a common tree
to ram is to crash into, so a ram is a collision

explanation.surface: Someone escapes from a tree just before a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for a quiet religious refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermitage or religious community in India is a place of spiritual withdrawal from the world.

clue.text: Cleaner admitting general public to dance venue

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a broom is a sweeping implement for cleaning
all, as in everyone, the general public

explanation.surface: A janitor lets the whole public into a dance hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hall designed for formal dancing is exactly this kind of venue.

clue.text: We supply milk to de rest

definitions.text: We supply milk to de rest

parts.words: We supply milk to de rest
parts.note: the dairy organs speak, and 'de rest' in comic dialect is 'the others', said like the answer

explanation.walkthrough: 'De rest' mimics an accent that turns 'the others' into something like 'de udders', giving a second reading of the cow's milk organs.
explanation.definitionFit: The milk-producing glands of cows and goats are the ones that supply milk to everyone else.

clue.text: Alternative information given out on companion animals

indicators.note: on places the alternative after the companion in the answer

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
or introduces an alternative
data is information supplied or given out

explanation.surface: Different facts are released about a friend's pets.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the phylum name at the end, not the companion animals of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The phylum of animals with a backbone or notochord is a zoological grouping of creatures.

clue.text: Sequential article on board ship

indicators.note: on board means inside the vessel, so the article goes within the ship

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An orderly piece of writing on a voyage aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' places A within LINER.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged in a line, one after another, describes something sequential.

clue.text: Souls in hell receiving 6 of 2

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, hell
VI is the Roman numeral six
dual means of or relating to two

explanation.surface: Sinners in the inferno take on numbers from other clues.
explanation.walkthrough: The '6 of 2' looks like cross-references to other entries but is just Roman six and a word meaning 'of two'.
explanation.definitionFit: Souls can mean people, as in 'not a soul', so persons counted singly fit.

clue.text: Express letters sure to get one fascinated

parts.note: to spell a word is to express its letters
bound, as in 'bound to', means sure

explanation.surface: Someone receives special delivery mail and is thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express letters' suggests urgent post, but it is the verb to spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held entranced as though by a charm is enthralled or captivated.

clue.text: A parent to one without?

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal, a parent

explanation.surface: A mother or father figure to a person left with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first man had no parents, so he is one 'without' a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Biblical first man was created, not born, so he had no mother or father.

clue.text: A Pope-supporting circle? Not entirely

parts.note: RC is Roman Catholic, the church loyal to the Pope

explanation.surface: Is a group loyal to the Pope only half-hearted?
explanation.definitionFit: A curved section of a circumference is part of a circle but not the whole.

clue.text: Lust, perhaps, so sadly admitted by one entering place of iniquity

annotationWithheld.why: Lust, perhaps, so sadly admitted by one entering place of iniquity (6,3): DEN takes ADLYS plus I, but ADLYS is 'sadly' rearranged and the only word to signal that is 'sadly' itself, doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Lust, perhaps, so sadly admitted by one entering place of iniquity

clue.text: A second coffee knocked back in aid of crime

parts.note: B is second in the alphabet

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, here read as the word turned backwards

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: A further coffee is downed as part of planning a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A second' suggests a moment of time, but 'second' is B; 'knocked back' reads as drunk quickly, here turning the coffee round.
explanation.definitionFit: Abetting, helping or encouraging wrongdoing, is assistance given to an offence.

clue.text: Intelligence is lacking in one's cups

indicators.note: is lacking means the following letters are missing from the word

parts.note: brain means intelligence

explanation.surface: Someone in their cups has lost their wits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in one's cups' means drunk, but here the cups are those of a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassiere is the undergarment made of a pair of cups.

clue.text: One succeeding stifles account that's less than precise

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: stifles means smothers, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: next means following, succeeding

explanation.surface: A successor suppresses a vague report of events.
explanation.definitionFit: Not exact means imprecise, short of accuracy.

clue.text: Cinerama represents the Beauty of Film

indicators.note: represents here means re-presents, the letters presented again in a new order

explanation.surface: A widescreen format shows a cinema classic.
explanation.walkthrough: Cinerama was a widescreen cinema process; the film is 'American Beauty' (1999), so the Beauty of Film is American.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1999 Oscar-winning movie's title pairs the word Beauty with this nationality adjective.

clue.text: Auditor's opponents fixed up fragments

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: an auditor is a listener, the organ being the ear
East and South are opposing partnerships at bridge
set means fixed

explanation.surface: A listener's adversaries repaired some broken pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns EARESSET into the answer. 'Auditor' suggests an accountant, but it is a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Small cubes of stone or glass used in mosaic are tiny pieces of a larger work.

clue.text: Breathe irregularly when interrupting doctor

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A patient pants while breaking in on a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: To pant or draw a sudden breath is to breathe in a fitful way.

clue.text: Energy and charm left out of sacred text

parts.note: go means energy or vigour

indicators.note: out of means the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a spell is a magic charm

explanation.surface: Vigour and allure are missing from holy writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the four accounts of Christ's life in the New Testament is a holy book.

clue.text: Flight of the last of the Jedi into galaxy

indicators.note: into means put inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a galaxy is a system of stars

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A Star Wars knight's escape into the galaxy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests escape or air travel, but it is a set of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps is a run of them between floors.

clue.text: Nun kissed Newton out of spite

indicators.note: out of order, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: N is the symbol for the newton, a unit of force

explanation.surface: A nun kissed Isaac Newton purely out of malice.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkindness, ill will towards others, is close to malice.

clue.text: Big-bummed beatnik?

definitions.meaning: a beatnik was a bohemian forerunner of the flower-power generation

explanation.definitionFit: A wide-hipped person and a 1960s flower child share this spelling.

clue.text: Bolshevik name joins revised A-list

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A Bolshevik's name is added to a reworked list of celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet dictator was a leading member of the Bolshevik revolutionaries.

clue.text: For whom hubby finally, and with regret, turned round to take great risk

definitions.text: For whom hubby finally, and with regret, turned round to take great risk

indicators.note: turned round means the word is read the other way about

parts.note: rue means regret

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

parts.note: to dice, as in dicing with death, is to take a big risk

explanation.surface: A tale of a husband who looked back at last, ruefully, and gambled everything.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Orpheus led his wife from the underworld but turned to look back, so she was lost.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek myth's bride, lost when Orpheus looked back, is the woman he turned round for.

clue.text: Broken heart of sour rape victim

indicators.note: broken signals the letters are smashed and rearranged
the heart of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A heartbroken account of a bitter assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of sour' gives OU, which with RAPE is reworked. In Greek myth Zeus as a bull carried off Europa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Phoenician princess abducted by Zeus disguised as a bull was a mythical victim.

clue.text: Final demands of university backing a Sri Lankan? About time

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the time goes inside
backing means going backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: Tamils are a people of Sri Lanka

explanation.surface: Ultimatums from a college supporting a Sri Lankan, concerning timing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns A TAMIL into LIMATA, which goes around T.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin plural of a final non-negotiable demand; these are last-word terms.
